summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, atrial fibrillation, and recent pericarditis, was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and orthopnea. Imaging revealed bilateral pleural effusions and multifocal pneumonia, with the right effusion requiring drainage via chest tube. He was treated with a 7-day course of IV antibiotics and aggressive diuresis, transitioning to oral torsemide. His kidney function showed transient worsening consistent with acute tubular necrosis, prompting an increase in tacrolimus dose. Diarrhea during admission was non-infectious and resolved. He improved clinically, with resolution of respiratory symptoms and stabilization of volume status, and was discharged home with follow-up plans including repeat imaging, a sleep study, and strict fluid and sodium restriction.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Acute kidney failure with tubular necrosis
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
